inputs.text: The Wisconsin jury was right to draw a hard line: requesting ballots for Robin Vos and Cory Mason without their consent was not election oversight, it was taking the law into one’s own hands. Harry Wait’s claim that he wanted to expose weaknesses doesn’t excuse identity theft or election fraud. But public trust also depends on officials answering legitimate questions plainly and ensuring the system can withstand scrutiny. When institutions expect confidence without transparency, suspicion grows; when citizens respond with illegal stunts, they make matters worse. Wait was convicted of two misdemeanor election-fraud charges and one felony identity-theft charge, and acquitted of another identity-theft count. Elections need both accountable officials and respect for the law.
